==Background==
Darwin the Devil was an outlaw, along with [[Archie the Kid]] and [[Robyn the Brute]].

He voted for [[Betty Pearson]] in the 2296 Overseer election. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FoTV vault 33 anxious dwellers.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Reg McPhee]] and Davey concerned about Lucy leaving the Vault]] Davey is briefly seen sitting among other [[Vault 33 dweller]]s who survived the [[Vault 32 raider]]s' attack on their Vault when [[Lucy MacLean]] proposes sending a team to search for her father on the surface. Soon after, he appears more prominently, pushing a wheelbarrow and assisting in the initial cleanup of the Vault, and is seen to have sustained a small wound on his forehead. He reacts with confusion when Norm greets him, saying that his day is going as "bad as everyone else's." He gives Norm another look of disbelief, shaking his head as he leaves. Davey and [[Reg McPhee|Reg]] witness [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] and [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] help [[Lucy MacLean]] leave [[Vault 33]]. They try to talk Lucy out of leaving, but fail to stop her. Davey comments blithely about this as Lucy leaves.{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Head]]==== Davey offers to teach the captured prisoners from [[Lee Moldaver]]'s raiders about [[William Shakespeare]], as well as [[Christopher Marlowe]], "when they are ready."{{FOTV|1|3}} ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:Vault 33 election.png|thumb|250px|Davey is voting for Betty]] Davey participates in voting for a new Vault 33 overseer, and while in line, he apologizes to Reg and initially alludes to him that he's voting for [[Betty Pearson|Betty]] instead of him. On the other hand, Reg understands, and when Davey informs Reg that he's voting for Betty, Reg states that he had that impression.{{FOTV|1|5}} [[File:Davey and Woody.png|thumb|250px|left|Davey and Woody after the election]] Afterward, Davey would console a forlorn [[Woody Thomas|Woody]], who was reeling over his election loss to Betty. He'd relate with Woody over his election loss, detailing he ran once, but lost against [[Hank MacLean|Hank]]. Davey would then recite the [[Vault 31]] phrase, "When things look glum, vote for someone from Vault 31". Before leaving, Davey again confesses that he voted for Betty to Woody. {{clear}} ====[[The Radio]]==== Davey discovers he will be relocating to Vault 32, which he positively reacts to. He moves into it with [[Steph Harper|Steph]], Chet and Woody. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== In contrast to his initial optimism, Davey reveals in a meeting with Steph, the new overseer, that he has been having difficulties navigating through the Vault due to its layout being a mirror of 33's, such as now having to take two left turns instead of two rights to reach the elevator. Despite Steph's attempt to end the meeting quickly, Davey continues by suggesting hanging some signage, then begins rambling about avoiding controversy by instead commissioning a feasibility study on signage, which the overseer frustratedly agrees to. As he leaves the overseer's office and makes small chat with [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] holding [[Chet Jr.]], Davey remarks on his "good fortune" to have found a wife and a child to raise despite Chet's protests against both of those facts. Davey exits the office foyer but turns to face a wall where he thought there was a hallway and has to turn around. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Davey is reading a book in his quarters when Woody accidentally walks in. Woody apologizes, citing difficulties getting used to their new home's layout; Davey sympathizes, recalling that he once accidentally walked into the women's men's room, which was fortunately empty. He then remarks that he would prefer living back in Vault 33. ====[[The Other Player]]==== Davey asks [[Irv]] if he has seen Woody, as they were due to play checkers that morning but Woody is nowhere to be found. As Chet called him over, Davey asks him if he wants to know the truth. Pulling up a chair, he confesses that he doesn't even like checkers and only plays it to keep Woody happy. Irv suggests they report Woody's disappearance to the overseer, but Davey scoffs before quickly apologizing to Chet for offending his wife. Chet insists that Steph wasn't his wife, so Davey corrects himself to say that fiancee is more appropriate, giving Chet a knowing wink before walking off. Chet, in fact, did not know that Steph had arranged for him to be married to her the next day. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Davey later officiates Chet and Steph's wedding. However, when it comes time for Chet to say, "I do", he refuses, throwing off Davey, who misheard them at first and was about to pronounce them married. Chet admits he is only going through with the wedding in order to have witnesses to formally accuse Steph of killing Woody, claiming he found Woody's glasses in his and Steph's garbage disposal. Given the severity of the accusation, Davey asks to see his evidence, only for Chet to admit that he ended up destroying the evidence. Because of this, none of the dwellers believe Chet's accusation, with Davey attributing Chet's behavior to "cold feet." Chet then reveals that Steph was not born in Vault 31, that she is in fact over 200 years old, and that she is [[Canada|Canadian]], causing the vault dwellers to react with outrage; Davey snatches Steph's Canadian ID card from Chet's hand to examine for himself. Outed, Steph retreats to her office and seals herself inside, with Davey, Chet, and the other Vault 32 dwellers gathering outside soon after to demand Steph come out. ====[[The Strip]]==== Still gathered outside Steph's office, Davey tells the assembled Vault 32 dwellers that their actions will serve as a "strong message to management," and Irv declares after him that it should mean "death to management." Davey, Irv, and the other dwellers begin chanting this message, while Chet is left horrified, realizing that the situation is starting to resemble what happened to the previous residents of Vault 32. ==Personality== Davey presents himself as an educated man who is well-versed in the theatrical arts of [[William Shakespeare]] and [[Christopher Marlowe]], but he is also shown to be fretful and have a guilty conscience for even small acts of self-perceived betrayal. This is displayed when he confesses that he voted for Betty to Reg and Woody instead of them. After being transferred to Vault 32, Davey struggled to acclimate to his new surroundings, which were designed to mirror Vault 33, preferring to the familiarity of his old Vault. ==Appearances== Davey appears only {{In|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|3=103|5=105|7=107|9=201|12=204|14=206|15=207|16=208}} ==Gallery== Davey's assignment.png|Davey learns of his new assignment ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault 32 characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]]
